slot.brief: integrate a proper rational function using partial fractions (distinct linear factors) via the cover-up technique

stem: Evaluate the integral of dx / (x^2 + x - 6).

verdicts.working: Factor x²+x−6=(x−2)(x+3). Partial fractions give 1/(x²+x−6)=(1/5)[1/(x−2)−1/(x+3)], whose integral is (A).

working:
Factor denominator: x^2 + x - 6 = (x - 2)(x + 3). Partial fractions give 1/[(x - 2)(x + 3)] = 1/[5(x - 2)] - 1/[5(x + 3)]. Integration gives (1/5) ln|x - 2| - (1/5) ln|x + 3| + C = (1/5) ln|(x - 2)/(x + 3)| + C.

Independent check: Factor x²+x−6=(x−2)(x+3). Partial fractions give 1/(x²+x−6)=(1/5)[1/(x−2)−1/(x+3)], whose integral is (A).
solution:
Factor the denominator and use partial fractions:
$$\frac{1}{(x-2)(x+3)}=\frac{1}{5}\left(\frac{1}{x-2}-\frac{1}{x+3}\right).$$
Hence, the integral is $\frac{1}{5}\ln|x-2|-\frac{1}{5}\ln|x+3|+C=\frac{1}{5}\ln\left|\frac{x-2}{x+3}\right|+C$.
